t:
(a) In General.—Subparagraph (A) of section 864(e)(5) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following: “Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, a foreign corporation shall be treated as a member of the affiliated group if—“(i) more than 50 percent of the gross income of such foreign corporation for the taxable year is effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United States, and“(ii) at least 80 percent of either the vote or value of all outstanding stock of such foreign corporation is owned directly or indirectly by members of the affiliated group (determined with regard to this sentence).”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section amends a tax rule on when a foreign corporation is treated as a member of an affiliated group and sets an effective date. The tempting reading is that "member of the affiliated group" signals some participatory body, but it is a corporate tax classification, not a process involving outside parties in a federal decision. There is no rulemaking, comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: a foreign corporation shall be treated as a member of the affiliated group if

opus.w: This section changes a definition in the Internal Revenue Code about when a foreign corporation counts as part of an affiliated group, and sets an effective date. Here "member" refers to corporate ownership, not to anyone outside the government taking part in a federal decision. The section does not authorize rulemaking or set up any consultation, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue, so it does not count as participation.
opus.s: a foreign corporation shall be treated as a member of the affiliated group if

1. **Reasoning:** The tempting misreading comes from the words "member" and "affiliated group." Here they only describe corporate ownership for a tax rule about allocating expenses. Nothing in the section asks for a comment period, rulemaking, a hearing, an advisory body, consultation, or a right to sue. No outside party takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Internal Revenue Code to define when a foreign corporation is treated as a member of an affiliated group for tax purposes. It establishes objective criteria (gross income connection and stock ownership) that are applied by the government without any requirement for consultation, coordination, or input from the foreign corporations or any other outside parties. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or consultation with states/tribes involved in this specific provision.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute defines how foreign corporations are treated for tax purposes, it involves "participation" of those corporations in the tax system. However, the definition of participation requires consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties *before* a federal decision is made. This section merely sets out statutory criteria for tax classification; it does not require the government to consult with the corporations, the public, or any other outside entity before applying these rules. The corporations are subjects of the regulation, not participants in the decision-making process.
